title: Japan residence fees rise October 1; September 30 is the old-fee cutoff
summary: Japan's Immigration Services Agency has published the detailed October 1, 2026 residence-permission fee schedule. Applications accepted by September 30 remain under the old fee schedule, while October applications face materially higher change, renewal and permanent-residence costs.
why_it_matters: This expands ALAM's earlier alert with the full practical fee and payment details. Foreign residents whose normal filing window is already open can now estimate the cost difference, but the cutoff is not a reason to submit an incomplete or premature application.

claims.text: The revised fees apply to residence-status change, period-of-stay renewal and permanent-residence applications accepted on or after October 1, 2026; applications accepted by September 30 use the old fee even if permission is issued later.
claims.basis: Immigration Services Agency effective-date and transition rule

claims.text: For online change or renewal applications accepted from October 1, the total payment including the settlement fee ranges from ¥10,330 for a period of three months or less to ¥65,550 for five years or more.
For counter applications from October 1, change and renewal fees range from ¥10,000 to ¥75,000 depending on the permitted period, and permanent residence is ¥200,000.
claims.basis: Official revised fee and revenue-stamp guidance

claims.text: Online payments from October use the designated convenience-store or bank settlement process; credit cards and QR-code payments are not supported under the published procedure.
Qualifying severe economic hardship or other special circumstances may support a reduced or waived fee, but the reduction process is handled at the counter rather than through online filing.

A person whose filing window is already open and whose application is complete can potentially avoid a substantial fee increase by filing before the September 30 acceptance cutoff, but fee savings alone are not a reason to submit an incomplete or strategically premature case.
claims.basis: Inference from the transition rule and published fee schedule

change_summary.previous: ALAM's first version established that change and renewal fees become period-based from October 1, that online totals can rise sharply, and that applications accepted by September 30 keep the old fee.
change_summary.now: Official implementation detail adds the counter fee range, the ¥200,000 permanent-residence fee, the online settlement method and the counter-only hardship reduction route.
change_summary.why_change_matters: Affected residents can now estimate the likely administrative cost and choose the correct filing/payment route while still treating September 30 as a cost cutoff rather than a reason to rush an unready case.

content.key_message: If your residence renewal, status change or permanent-residence application is already legitimately ready, September 30 is the last acceptance date for the old fee schedule; October 1 brings substantially higher fees.
content.who_is_affected: Foreign residents planning a residence-status change, period-of-stay renewal or permanent-residence application around late September or October 2026.
content.when: New fees apply to applications accepted from October 1, 2026. Applications accepted by September 30 remain under the old fee schedule even if the decision comes later.
content.financial_impact: Online change/renewal totals run from ¥10,330 to ¥65,550 under the new schedule. Counter change/renewal fees run from ¥10,000 to ¥75,000 depending on the permitted period, and permanent residence is ¥200,000.
content.risk_if_ignored: An otherwise-ready application that crosses into October acceptance can cost materially more. The opposite risk is rushing an incomplete or premature immigration application merely to chase the old fee.
content.deadline: September 30, 2026 is the final acceptance date for the old fee schedule, but only file if the normal filing window is open and the application is genuinely ready.
content.effort: Medium: confirm eligibility and timing, complete the normal procedure-specific documents, choose the valid filing route and retain acceptance evidence.
content.potential_benefit: Potentially avoids tens of thousands of yen in new fees for a case that was already due and ready to file.
content.downside: An early, incomplete or incorrect application can create more serious administrative risk than the fee increase.
content.what_would_change_mind: A later Immigration Services Agency notice delaying implementation, changing the acceptance-date transition rule or revising the published fee tables.
